name: JD Cables Limited
summary: JD Cables is a small cable/conductor manufacturer undergoing a material shift into civil/electrical EPC subcontracting. Production, reported earnings and commissioned capacity have grown rapidly, but profit has not converted into operating cash for three consecutive years. At the 19 October 2026 close of ₹176.05, this is an unresolved growth/execution special situation, not a proven compounder or an established distress/default case. BQS is 4.96 (display 5.0), GQS is 6.25 capped at 5.0 by persistent cash weakness, and IAS is NS. The ₹83 crore credit sanction is meaningful favorable evidence: restrained completion can fit it, so G3 is Hold, not Fail. However, current drawable funding and committed EPC cash-to-complete are unknown, and the ordinary growth base exceeds the facility ceiling. Even an explicitly hypothetical dilutive rescue base earns only 12.39% against a 15% hurdle. Verify funded collections, contractual commitments and current BSE tradeability before a price-based investment conclusion. [E1–E4,E10,E16–E20]

GOV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Auditor gives unmodified opinion and no reported default/fraud; historical small tax demands are disclosed, not treated as criminal findings.
Director remuneration is about 1.06% of PAT, and promoter lending carries disclosed 6% interest.

GOV.contrary_evidence: Bank-filed asset/liability amounts differ from audited books; classification corrigendum and IPO fee allocation reduce reporting confidence.
GOV.reason: Adequate conduct with explainable material control/disclosure concerns, not substantiated minority abuse. No governance override.
GOV.boundary: Not 4 without recurrent harmful stewardship or abuse evidence; not 6 while stock-statement reconciliation, current related terms and post-IPO disclosure quality remain unsettled.

MOAT.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Top-five FY25 customers supply about 63.88% of revenue and orders are not guaranteed recurring contracts.
Cable/conductor production is contestable; established relevant peers have 3.3–5.2 times JD sales and stronger cash realization.

MOAT.contrary_evidence: Utility vendor approvals and experience across several states create useful qualification friction.
MOAT.reason: Qualifications do not yet demonstrate sustained pricing power, exclusive demand or resilient excess economics. Does not penalize cash again.
MOAT.boundary: 4 rather than 3 recognizes manufacturing qualifications and production history; 5 needs demonstrable retained customers/qualification economics rather than merely a listed client roster.

REV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Selected three-year FY23–FY26 revenue CAGR is 107.42%, starting score 9; five-year reliable data unavailable.
Physical-km CAGR is about 80.99%; FY26 named cable/conductor revenue grows 33.35%, crosschecking substantial underlying scale rather than acquisitions alone.

REV.contrary_evidence: FY26 physical km grows only 4.15%; price/mix and the new EPC residual materially inflate reported revenue growth.
REV.reason: No trajectory adjustment from one preliminary quarter. Growth basis is reported organic enterprise revenue with physical/product crosschecks, no purchased business. Medium/four-year history ceiling reduces 9 to 8.
REV.boundary: 9 is barred by short reliable history and imperfect price/volume separation. 7 would require weakening the demonstrated multi-year expansion beyond disclosed mix effects, not a second small-base penalty.

DUR.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Two new production lines commissioned before cutoff and declared capacity doubles to 56,000 km.
Executed EPC awards and recent cable orders establish access beyond an unsupported industry TAM.

DUR.contrary_evidence: New-product certifications, new EPC execution capability, customer concentration and cash-to-complete constrain accessible runway.
DUR.reason: Multiple concrete avenues exist, but repeatable multi-year conversion and approvals are not yet demonstrated.
DUR.boundary: 6 substantially meets mixed/adequate runway. 7 requires verified utilization, product approvals and diversified repeat orders; 5 would underweight commissioned capacity and signed work.

CAP.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: FY26 average-capital normalized ROIC is 24.90%, but latest incremental return is only 7.77% (7.48% on stricter economic EBIT).
Two-year incremental return is 16.48%; IPO and new assets precede full capacity earnings.

CAP.contrary_evidence: Commissioned capacity could improve cohort returns; high average ROIC is real but not proof of high returns on new capital.
CAP.reason: Mixed cohorts around/below a reasoned 12–15% capital-cost range, with insufficient mature new-plant economics. This is a return-on-capital assessment, not a duplicate CFO deduction.
CAP.boundary: 4 would require persistent below-cost cohort economics rather than one transition year. 6 needs improved utilization and incremental NOPAT on the enlarged capital base.

CASH.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: FY24–26 cumulative CFO is −₹104.4677 crore on ₹58.3294 crore PAT, with all three years negative.
FY26 inventories, receivables, advances and EMD absorb capital while supplier credit declines; capex is additional to this operating outflow.

CASH.contrary_evidence: FY26 AR ageing is mostly under six months and FY23 CFO was positive; no audited doubtful/contested balance is reported.
CASH.reason: Persistent severe cash-conversion weakness is evidenced before and after EPC, not assumed fraud or total bad debt. Apply GQS persistent CASH≤3 cap at 5.
CASH.boundary: 2 rather than 1 recognizes reported ageing and the possibility of investment-driven recovery; 3 needs demonstrated collections and reduction of cumulative funding absorption, not merely guidance.

BAL.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: ₹83 crore sanctioned facilities and BBB/Stable credit assessment are genuine favorable funding evidence; March theoretical undrawn amount ₹37.2958 crore.
Restrained central essential case fits within ₹83 crore, even at 8% core margin, assuming drawability and timing.

BAL.contrary_evidence: Virtually no free cash, on-demand revolving facilities and unknown EPC/land commitments leave material stress sensitivity; 40% project funding intensity breaches the limit.
BAL.reason: Manageable under stated central availability assumptions but not robust enough for a stronger resilience score. G3 Hold is uncertainty, not an asserted default.
BAL.boundary: 4 would require a supported likely essential shortfall rather than an optional-growth funding gap. 6 requires confirmed drawing power, maturity/renewal and a monthly remaining-project cash schedule.

EXEC.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: New conductor and cable operations commenced in July and September; completed land conveyance verifies a physical asset rather than only plans.
Core production grew from 3,972 km FY23 to 23,549 km FY26.

EXEC.contrary_evidence: June expected electricity/start timing slipped into July and cable timing into September; EPC certification/completion against nine/twelve-month terms is not verified.
EXEC.reason: Real expansion delivery with modest delays and unproven EPC adaptation; no basis for claiming either consistent excellence or a defaulted contract.
EXEC.boundary: 6 needs delivery and collection milestones on the major EPC commitments; 4 would need evidenced repeated serious misses rather than small documented slippage and unknown status.

EARN.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Other income ₹0.6021 crore is small versus PBT ₹42.4672 crore; most reported growth is operating, not asset-sale gains.
PAT grows about 44%, but year-end-share analytical EPS grows only 5.71% after pre-IPO/IPO dilution; H2 normalized EBITDA margin falls to 11.69%.

EARN.contrary_evidence: FY26 annual EBITDA ex OI remains 13.03%, and current common-share-basis earnings progress is strong.
EARN.reason: Operating profit growth is credible but product/EPC mix, dilution and unproven EPC execution prevent a high recurring per-share-quality score. CASH handles conversion separately.
EARN.boundary: 5 would understate operating earnings progress; 7 requires repeatable diluted per-share progress and margin resilience through the EPC transition.

R.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Ordinary base exceeds the assumed existing credit ceiling and therefore has no valid IRR.
The separately identified dilutive rescue base returns 12.39%, below the 15% hurdle, but its financing is not committed.

R.contrary_evidence: Bull and restrained diagnostics can be funded under explicit current-facility and collection assumptions; the restrained diagnostic returns 7.19%.
R.reason: NS is not mechanically caused by G3 Hold: essential project financing/timing remains quantitatively unresolved and spans funded/unfunded outcomes. The 7.19% alternative is not the most supported economic base and cannot establish a robust R2 for the actual evolving business. If rescue financing were independently established, 12.39% would map to R4, not a neutral 5.
R.boundary: Requires current drawable facilities, remaining signed project/capital obligations and a credible funded operating base. No averaging of scenarios or assigning a point to an unfunded case.

D.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Credible ordinary bear has a ₹72.19 crore peak funding gap and no supported shareholder IRR.
A counterfactual equity rescue produces −11.90% annual return and about 46.93% terminal price loss before execution costs.

D.contrary_evidence: Central restrained essential completion fits sanctioned credit; unmodified audit and BBB rating argue against assuming zero recovery/default.
D.reason: Material impairment and adverse recapitalization risk, not a proved unavoidable bankruptcy. Scenario assumptions are explicit and not assigned probabilities.
D.boundary: 3 is the lower material-risk band; 4 would need tighter funding/contract-loss bounds, while 2 would overstate evidence of inevitable inadequate essential funding.

P.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Entry is about 12.51x FY26 PAT and 9.55x EBITDA ex OI, not an obvious high-multiple hype valuation.
At 12% margin and 7x exit, the reverse model needs roughly 14.00% FY28–32 growth after FY27 ₹550 crore, plus a dilutive raise, to earn 15%.

P.contrary_evidence: A 10% growth rescue base returns only 12.39%; reducing margin and exit multiple can erase returns.
P.reason: The price broadly requires an execution case, but affords limited allowance for funding and margin error. No peer rerating justified without common-date peer valuations.
P.boundary: 5 recognizes fair rather than fantastic operating expectations; 6 requires a verified funded base close to hurdle, 4 would need more aggressive joint assumptions than currently implied.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
JD Cables Limited; BSE SME scrip 544524 / JDCABLES; ISIN INE14VP01014. It is not an NSE-listed issuer merely because an NSE interoperability master contains JDCABLES$. Information cutoff: 20 October 2026. Quote: historical 19 October close ₹176.05, not a live execution promise. Official dated shares 22,551,112 imply equity value ₹397.0123 crore; lot 800 implies ₹140,840 per lot. Standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards; no subsidiary/associate/JV/NCI in the audited scope. Rent remains an operating expense, with no invented Ind AS lease liability. [S1,M1,M2]

Five-year investment period is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, nominal INR, common equity hurdle 15%, reference position ₹5 lakh, not a suitable allocation recommendation. Latest audited balance-sheet opening is 31 March 2026, so April–October cash flows are unobserved forecast bridge, not known entry-date cash. FY27 preliminary Q1 revenue is not audited H1 earnings/cash. [S1,S12]

Liquidity: all 60 expected BSE sessions from July 24 to October 19 have actual secondary turnover, with no missing or observed zero-trade days. Mean ₹1,01,57,751.33 and median ₹81,00,020 make the lower median the formal reference. ₹5 lakh theoretical exit days are 3.0864 / 1.2346 / 0.6173 at 2% / 5% / 10% participation. The 20-session mean/median are ₹91,26,662 / ₹80,65,120, giving 1.2399 days at 5%. These are capacity estimates, not executable quotes. Three/four lots are ₹4,22,520/₹5,63,360; each requires about two median whole-lot-capacity sessions at 5%. Five of 60 sessions cannot fit even one lot at 5%, and 31–32 at 2%. Exact current effective free float, spread, bid depth and locked-circuit history remain ND. March nonpromoter shares are not necessarily available float. Capacity starting L9 and conditional implementation L8 are not formal clearance. [M1,M2; liquidity packet]

G1 Clear; G2 Conditional; G3 Hold—unresolved essential funding; G4 Hold—unresolved current implementation. High confidence in audited FY26 totals, dated facility sanction and official shares/lot; Medium in short comparable growth history, normalized economics, peers and secondary turnover; Low/ND in October drawing power, full EPC terms, post-March obligations, latest scanned shareholding and executable depth. Retrieval after cutoff uses only pre-cutoff documents and dated historical prices. [Gate register; source ledger]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 6; R NS, D 3, P 5, L NS. Every factor has two material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and a neighboring-score explanation in factor_audit.json.

BQS = 1.00 + 0.80 + 0.96 + 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.20 + 0.40 + 0.40 = 4.96; 100% coverage, Medium aggregate confidence; display 5.0. GQS = 3.20 + 1.20 + 0.90 + 0.75 + 0.20 = 6.25; persistent CASH≤3 caps final at 5.0. No governance or funding-Fail cap is applied. REV starts at 9 for ≥30% CAGR, no trajectory adjustment, reduced to 8 by the Medium/four-year history ceiling.

IAS known contribution = 0.25×4.96 + 0.20×3 + 0.10×5 = 2.34. Missing R and L weights total 45%; coverage 55%; mathematical missing-data bound 2.79–6.84, not a confidence interval or rankable point. Conditional L8 only narrows the mathematical bound to 3.49–6.64; it does not supply current implementation clearance. If rescue financing were proven, its 12.39% IRR would map to R4, but that is not the actual supported base. No neutral substitutions or weight redistribution.

GOV and CAP each ±1 move BQS jointly to 4.64–5.28; GQS remains capped at 5.0. This stays within the same 4≤BQS<6 matrix quality band, although nearby provisional numerical rankings may change. Displayed 5.0 does not replace unrounded 4.96 in calculations. All batch comparisons remain provisional until the full universe is complete.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
JD manufactures power/control/aerial-bunched and related cables and conductors, primarily serving Indian utilities, EPC contractors and industrial customers from its West Bengal plants. Its disclosed supply footprint spans eastern/northeastern states as well as Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan; audited foreign-currency export earnings are nil. Customer qualification and tender procurement, metal inputs, manufacturing conversion and timely dispatch drive product economics. Collection is not point-of-sale cash: supplier advances, inventories, customer credit and performance/security deposits tie up money. [S1,S2]

FY26 presentation product sales were cables/wires ₹252.5632 crore and conductors ₹81.5235 crore, against ₹202.1327/48.3931 crore FY25. Their ₹30.5048 crore residual to total revenue is consistent with management's approximately ₹30 crore EPC revenue, not a formally audited standalone EPC segment-profit result. Contractor charges of ₹17.6010 crore appear in FY26 other expenses. Since December 2025, JD has taken two large back-to-back civil/electrical EPC subcontracts from Kaushal Engineering for Jharkhand work. This introduces certification, subcontractor, retention, mobilization and execution risks beyond cable manufacturing. [S1,S4–S6,S8]

The two EPC announcements total ₹406.8712 crore including 18% GST, or ₹344.8061 crore net. Subtracting the management ₹30 crore FY26 estimate leaves ₹314.8061 crore to complete, subject to actual recognition/variation updates. New orders are not cash or recurring franchise revenue; gross GST-inclusive order value must not be equated to reported sales. [S4,S5,S8]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible moat is qualification and supplier execution reliability, not a demonstrated consumer brand or proprietary technology. State-utility vendor approval, product standards and manufacturing experience can slow a new entrant, but customers can tender among qualified vendors. FY25 top-five customers accounted for 63.88% of revenue (FY24 73.14%; FY23 45.29%); the RHP discloses no assured long-term purchase contracts. This concentration weakens evidence for pricing power. EPC adds a concentrated principal-contractor relationship rather than automatically diversifying economic risk. [S2,E9,E10]

Relevant FY26 operating peers, all in ₹ crore: JD revenue 364.59, EBITDA ex OI 47.51 (13.03%), CFO/PAT −2.32x, gross debt/equity 0.39x; Dynamic Cables 1,197.82 / 129.56 (10.82%) / 0.73x / 0.09x; V-Marc consolidated 1,797.31 / 200.83 (11.17%) / 1.09x / 0.74x; Paramount standalone 1,912.16 / 65.73 (3.44%) / −0.70x, exact borrowing/equity not recovered. All financial rows are FY26; V-Marc consolidation difference is explicit. Paramount's ₹51.77 crore other income is excluded rather than mistaking headline profitability for operating margin. Dynamic's printed net-debt arithmetic is not used; gross borrowing/equity is reconstructed. [S1,P1–P3; peer_memo.json]

JD's accounting margin is not evidence of an impregnable moat when cash realization is much poorer and EPC economics are new. Conversely, weak cash is not used as a second arbitrary MOAT deduction: the score 4 rests on contestability and concentration. No peer valuation premium/discount is asserted without common-date prices, shares and EV scope. Failure modes are qualification loss, aggressive tender pricing, metal-price/mix change and a large buyer shifting orders.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reliable audited/restated history is FY23–FY26, not five invented years. Revenue progresses ₹40.8554 → ₹100.8333 → ₹250.5258 → ₹364.5915 crore; annual increases are ₹59.9779, ₹149.6925 and ₹114.0657 crore, or 146.81%, 148.46% and 45.53%. The preselected three-year CAGR is 107.42%. FY21/FY22 primary scans were found but could not be extracted reliably, so five-year CAGR is ND. No purchased-business acquisition is identified; growth comes from organic product sales and entry into EPC, not an acquired turnover add-on. [S1,S2,S18]

Physical production grows 3,972 → 11,504.2 → 22,610 → 23,549 km, about 80.99% three-year CAGR but only 4.15% FY26 growth. Kilometers do not hold conductor gauge/product mix constant. FY26 cable/wire revenue grows 24.95%, conductor revenue 68.46%, combined named products 33.35%, while EPC supplies an additional residual. Thus FY26's 45.53% headline growth is not a volume-growth claim. Metal realization, richer product mix and new contracts matter; exact tonnage and realization decomposition is ND. [S1,S2,S6]

H2 FY26 revenue is ₹243.3362 crore versus ₹143.0506 crore (+70.11%); derived H1 revenue ₹121.2553 crore versus ₹107.4752 crore (+12.82%). H2 EBITDA excluding OI is ₹28.4476 crore, margin 11.69%, versus 13.16% in H2 FY25. H2 is a half-year balancing figure, not four independent quarters. Preliminary Q1 FY27 revenue ₹81.81 crore versus ₹48.78 crore (+67.71%) and September/October orders support activity, but neither validates cash nor earns an extra REV point. REV is 8 after the history/confidence ceiling. [S6,S12–S14]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Bottom-up access is tangible: old capacity 28,000 km at FY26 unit utilizations 82.43% and 84.56%; new conductor and cable units commissioned July/September with declared combined capacity 56,000 km. Higher-voltage/new conductor products require approvals and licenses before meaningful utilization. Existing ₹344.81 crore ex-GST EPC awards add execution workload, while management described approximately ₹500 crore total book in June and more than ₹1,000 crore tenders participated in. Tender participation is not awarded backlog; snapshots and later wins cannot be mechanically summed. [S1,S6,S8,S10,S11]

Management's June primary guidance was 50–60% revenue growth in FY27 and FY28, minimum ₹200 crore EPC FY27, about 8% EPC PAT margin, clarified to approximately 12–13% EBITDA on transcript page 14, and conditional ₹20–30 crore capex. Adjacent-land advances had already been paid; remaining contractual consideration is unknown. The ordinary analytical base uses FY27 ₹550 crore, then only 10% annual growth, not a wholesale adoption of this guidance. Its companywide EBITDA is 11.5% then 12%, an analyst haircut for execution risk, not a false 8% EBITDA attribution. At flat 12%/13% EBITDA, ordinary base still has ₹25.45/21.19 crore financing gaps; conditional equity-rescue IRRs are 12.53%/15.18%. The upper credible margin can meet the hurdle, but not without the assumed recapitalization and collections. Even so, working capital and capital expenditure push required bank debt beyond current sanction. Restrained survival strips out discretionary new tenders and expansion but retains signed work, opening claims and a bound for remaining land obligations. [S8; model.py]

Latest incremental ROIC is 7.77% (7.48% keeping late-tax interest/loan-processing charges in operating cost), below the assumed 12–15% capital-cost range, versus two-year incremental 16.48%. The enlarged IPO-funded denominator and plant commissioning lag explain why these are mixed cohorts rather than proof of permanent value destruction. Demand access earns DUR6, mixed capital returns CAP5, while independently severe cash realization CASH2 caps GQS from 6.25 to 5.0. A larger order book alone earns no growth-quality bonus. [E2,E7,E10–E13]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter Piyush Garodia and his mother held 15,786,414 shares at March 2026, approximately 70%; March filings report no pledge or convertible/options dilution. September filing is present but scanned details remain unverified; do not call this a current pledge clearance. Directors' remuneration totals ₹0.336 crore, about 1.06% of FY26 PAT; all disclosed key-management pay totals approximately ₹0.499 crore. Promoter loans ₹10.8812 crore carry 6% interest and are repayable on demand, a source of support but not free permanent equity. No cash dividend is assumed. [S1,S9]

The IPO had ₹84.41472 crore fresh gross company proceeds, not the additional ₹11.57632 crore OFS. Monitoring records ₹78.54 crore net fully used by March: ₹45 crore working capital, ₹26 crore debt repayment, ₹7.54 crore general purposes. Annual net equity cash proceeds ₹84.4598 crore reconcile to fresh gross plus ₹5.211284 crore pre-IPO proceeds less ₹5.16624 crore annual issue-cost charge. Monitor total fees exceed that charge by ₹0.70848 crore; possible offer/company allocation is not verified. Already spent proceeds cannot be treated as available cash again. [S1,S2,S7]

Promises versus delivery: October 13 land plan expected conveyance in about two months; deed registered December 23, modestly later. June call envisaged conductor electricity/start in June and cable production around two months thereafter; actual starts were July 6 and September 14. Plants therefore exist, with modest slippage. December EPC one-year and January EPC nine-month terms remain material: as of cutoff the latter nominal period has ended, but certified completion/extensions are not recovered. This is an open verification item, not a declared contractual default. [S4,S5,S8,S10,S11,S15,S16]

Control concerns: March inventory ₹78.8634 crore in books versus ₹68.4121 crore bank statements; AR ₹95.5615 versus ₹88.5592 crore; AP ₹22.4490 versus ₹27.2395 crore. Company explanation is provisional bank filings adjusted on finalization. Auditor remains unmodified and reports no fraud/default; no fabricated-loss or fraud inference is made. August 21 corrigendum fixes a short-term provision tagged long-term and promises more care. CFO subtotal labels and reported DSCR definitions also need care. FY25 unpaid CSR ₹4.82662 lakh was subsequently covered: FY26 ₹30 lakh spending exceeds combined requirement ₹28.18475 lakh, so an old uncured CSR allegation is inappropriate. RHP small tax matters are dated, not convictions; later auditor nil disputed-dues disclosure is favorable but not independent adjudication proof. [S1,S2,S17]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY23 / FY24 / FY25 / FY26, ₹ crore: revenue 40.8554 / 100.8333 / 250.5258 / 364.5915; PAT 0.3196 / 4.5798 / 22.0250 / 31.7246; CFO 1.2249 / −12.7469 / −18.2126 / −73.5082; cash capex 0 / 1.6316 / 7.2626 / 18.0612; equity 1.1816 / 7.8295 / 29.9861 / 146.1705; gross debt 3.8413 / 17.7691 / 45.9117 / 56.6255. FY25 uses the later FY26 audited comparative; RHP FY25 PAT ₹22.1530 crore is separately retained, not silently substituted. Prior-period expense ₹0.1351 crore and tax presentation explain most of the difference. [S1,S2; financial_history_enriched.json]

FY26 PBT ₹42.4672 + finance ₹4.3895 − OI ₹0.6021 gives EBIT ₹46.2546; plus D&A ₹1.2533 gives EBITDA ₹47.5079, 13.03%. A stricter economic EBIT of ₹45.5880 retains ₹0.4843 late-tax interest and ₹0.1823 loan-processing charges as operating costs; the comparable FY25 economic EBIT is ₹32.9259 after the same adjustment type (₹0.0342/0.1433 crore); economic EBITDA ₹46.8413. Presentation EBITDA ₹48.1101 includes OI and is not the normalized valuation numerator. Current tax ₹10.7982 crore and deferred credit ₹0.0556 crore imply effective tax about 25.30%; forward cash tax uses 25% of positive pretax profit. Materials and inventory movement create a ₹78.3243 crore value-added proxy before EPC contractor costs, not a clean manufacturing gross profit. [S1,S6]

CFO bridge: pre-working-capital operating cash ₹47.3685 crore minus working-capital absorption ₹107.5837 crore minus cash taxes ₹13.2930 crore = −₹73.5082 crore. The printed 'cash used in operations' ₹107.5837 crore is a working-capital subtotal, not the final pre-tax operating cash; arithmetic is preserved. Inventory grows ₹42.8142 crore, AR ₹34.7099 crore, current advances ₹24.9081 crore, noncurrent deposits/EMD ₹6.2074 crore, while AP falls ₹9.4809 crore. Average-receivable/total-sales day proxies are 63.97/62.85/78.29 for FY24/FY25/FY26; ending inventory/revenue days are 44.39/52.52/78.95. These are revenue-based indicators, not verified cost-based inventory days or a full CCC; GST and credit-sale scope can distort them. Three-year FCF after cash capex is −₹131.4231 crore. Finished goods ₹44.7314 crore and WIP ₹8.7211 crore make conversion monitoring especially important. Favorably, 99.16% of AR is reported under six months, no doubtful/disputed rows, and only ₹0.1176 crore is over a year; negative CFO alone is not proof of irrecoverability. [S1,E2,E3,E15]

Normalized NOPAT/average invested capital yields FY26 ROIC 24.90%, ending-capital ROIC 17.11%; latest incremental return is 7.77%, two-year 16.48%, and three-year 17.23%; a five-year measure is ND. Invested capital includes IPO funds: equity + all debt − only unrestricted cash, ₹202.7906 crore at March versus ₹75.8736 crore FY25. No capex/working-capital double addition. Approximate net debt/EBITDA is 1.19x, gross debt/equity 0.39x, and all-finance interest cover 10.54x. These good earnings ratios coexist with negligible cash. Free opening cash is ₹0.0054 crore, not reported cash/bank ₹0.5401 crore: ₹0.5346 crore deposits are maturity-restricted and/or collateral, without verified release. Note 17 versus cash-flow cash-in-hand differs by ₹1,000; the lower cash-flow cash figure is used, not a hidden material asset. Completed land/CWIP costs are not charged again. Remaining signed EPC, later land advances and unidentified contractual exposure receive explicit ranges instead of a fabricated nil claim. If any ₹18.8410 crore purchase advance is capital rather than operating, transfer to PPE is not a cash release: future capex means incremental cash only, and ONWC-release diagnostics depend on that unresolved composition. sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹176.05, equity capitalization ₹397.0123 crore plus March debt ₹56.6255 less unrestricted cash ₹0.0054 gives indicative EV ₹453.6324 crore: P/E 12.51x, EV/EBITDA ex OI 9.55x (economic 9.68x), price/book 2.72x and EV/sales 1.24x. These pair October price with March audited claims, not a current net-debt assertion. Negative CFO prevents a meaningful positive cash yield. Valuation is a five-year explicit financing/cash-flow bridge with normalized enterprise exit multiple, crosschecked by current earnings/book and reverse operating requirements, not a terminal multiple pasted onto unfinanced revenue. [S1,M1,M2; model.py]

Opening March 2026 flows through FY27–FY31 and a 202/365 FY32 stub to October 19 2031. FY32 stub cash revenue integrates a linear ramp from FY31 to the October run rate, rather than multiplying the higher FY32 rate by the whole stub. Terminal EBITDA uses the forward October run rate; entry-to-exit is exactly five years, no dividends. Future economic operating cash pays interest, tax, incremental ONWC, incremental capex and every opening claim once. Cash surpluses repay bank debt then accumulate. Terminal equity adds only accumulated cash and deducts bank/promoter debt and ₹0.1494 crore noncurrent gratuity; PPE/ONWC/collateral are not added on top of going-concern EV. No uncommitted new loan or IPO inflow finances the ordinary cases. [Model assumptions and claims ledger]

Ordinary bear/base/bull revenue paths FY27–FY32 are respectively ₹500/450/460/480/500/520, ₹550/605/665.5/732.05/805.255/885.7805, and ₹600/750/900/1035/1160/1276 crore. Bear EBITDA margins are 8%,7.5%,8%,8.5%,8.5%,8.5%, before a first-year ₹5 crore hypothetical overrun/LD sensitivity, which reduces first-year effective margin from 8% to 7%; base 11.5% then 12%; bull 13%. ONWC/revenue paths are bear 60→55%, base 48→42%, bull 40→38%; capex respectively ₹5/3/3/3/3/3, ₹20/10/8/10/10/12, and ₹20/15/18/20/20/20 crore. Exit multiples 5x/7x/9x. All scenarios retain remaining signed EPC in revenue/costs; recognition rolled into FY28 implicitly needs time extensions or tolerated delay. Extensions and actual completion are not verified, so the base/bull do not assert a penalty-free legal right to delay; the bear includes the separate ₹5 crore cost sensitivity. The essential-completion test instead costs all remaining signed work in one year. Later EPC wins are separate assumptions, not contracted backlog. [model_assumptions.json]

Assuming ₹83 crore drawable bank ceiling: ordinary bear peak required bank ₹155.19 crore, gap ₹72.19; ordinary base peak ₹110.58 crore, gap ₹27.58. Both IRRs are null, not zero or attractive returns. Bull peak bank ₹74.29 crore fits only if collection improvement and facility availability hold; modeled IRR 29.96% is not a supported base. A separate rescue counterfactual raises equity when required at ₹140.84, 20% below entry, with 2% fees: base gross ₹27.2683 crore, terminal shares 2.448723119 crore (+8.59%), terminal price ₹315.73, IRR 12.39%; bear gross ₹71.0344 crore, price ₹93.42, IRR −11.90%. These raises are not authorized, committed or predicted. They are assumed post-entry because the observed October issued-share count contains no rescue; the annual FY27 bridge does not prove financing was available before any intrayear peak. If a raise was required before entry, a separately verified bridge would be needed. [E17,E18]

Base rescue two-way sensitivity: at 5x/7x/9x, base margins produce 5.71%/12.39%/17.78% IRR; margins two points lower produce −0.43%/6.40%/11.82%; margins 1.5 points higher 9.66%/16.30%/21.70%. A separate ordinary-case grid recomputes funding requirements, not rescue dilution, for working-capital 40/44/48/52% against credit 45.7042/65/83/108 crore, with ₹108 crore expressly uncommitted. Entry/exit cost stresses of 1% and 3% reduce returns. No optimistic case hides its funding dependence.

Under the conditional rescue base only, hurdle-equivalent entry values at 12%/15%/18% are ₹179.15/156.97/138.01. This is not a safe-buy range before funding is established. A dynamic reverse model requires FY28–FY32 growth about 14.00% after FY27 ₹550 crore, terminal run-rate revenue ₹1,001.00 crore, 12% margin, 7x exit and the same uncommitted ₹27.27 crore raise to earn 15%. Alternatively a fixed-financing crosscheck needs about 7.92x exit; it is not a fully funded alternative growth solution. The reverse case holds productive capex fixed; proportionally scaling capex with the required revenue raises needed growth to 14.22% and terminal revenue to ₹1,009.90 crore. Neither is a validated capacity/mix plan. P5 reflects fair execution expectations with little funding/margin cushion; R remains NS because essential financing and a supported economic base are unresolved, not merely because a gate says Hold.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that JD is profitable, has commissioned assets, a BBB/Stable rating and recently enlarged ₹83 crore bank facilities; new-project working capital may be temporary rather than lost. It would be wrong to force G3 Fail by treating all sanction as unavailable, repaying all demand debt immediately, double-charging already-paid EMD/CWIP, or assuming all optional future growth must proceed. [S1,S3,S10,S11]

The essential test holds core sales flat at ₹334.5915 crore and completes all estimated ₹314.8061 crore remaining signed EPC, not just a convenient fraction. Core/EPC EBITDA margins are analyst stress assumptions of 10.5%/8%, not management guidance, maintenance ₹1.5 crore, no discretionary new tender or plant capex, no automatic release of existing ONWC, opening statutory/tax/current gratuity paid, car repaid and promoter debt retained. With ₹20 crore assumed opening EPC ONWC already deployed, 25% peak project capital intensity requires additional ₹58.7015 crore; project intensity includes receivables, retention, WIP, supplier credits and EMD. Required bank balance is ₹71.3358 crore, leaving ₹11.6642 crore against the sanction. At 40% intensity it becomes ₹120.0643 crore, a ₹37.0643 crore gap. Under management's clarified 12%/13% EPC EBITDA instead of the 8% analyst stress, central bank need falls to ₹61.59/59.15 crore. Those favorable sensitivities strengthen Hold rather than Fail, but neither verifies actual drawability or intramonth timing. The ₹11.6642 crore figure is bank headroom; incremental interest reduces the exact extra cash-commitment capacity to ₹11.3033 crore. Opening EPC allocation ₹10/20/30 crore and 15/25/40% intensities are shown, not asserted as known facts. [model_results.json essential_completion_grid]

Only half of March theoretical undrawn headroom available creates a ₹6.98 crore central gap; full availability clears it. Additional unquantified remaining land/other capital payment of ₹0/5/10/15 crore leads to bank ₹71.34/76.50/81.66/86.81 crore. A lower 8% core margin still fits at ₹77.81 crore; full promoter demand separately fits at ₹82.31 crore, leaving little cushion. These isolated sensitivities are not stacked into an unsupported catastrophe. Annual cash generation may arrive after the funding peak, so none proves intramonth survival without certificate/collection schedules. [Model essential sensitivities]

An alternative termination route, not added on top of full completion, tests hypothetical cash damages of 0/2.5/5% of remaining net EPC, ₹0/7.87/15.74 crore. Actual LD/cancellation/BG terms are unknown. Existing EMD ₹6.6712 crore is an already-paid asset at risk, not a fresh identical outflow. The ordinary lower-sales/margin/slower-collection bear needs recapitalization; its rescue loses about 46.93% of entry price before costs. The permanent-loss path is trapped project capital → constrained bank drawing power → interruption/claims or discounted equity → reduced per-share recovery. A hypothetical funding shortfall is not a recorded default. The thesis-break variable is certified cash collection and remaining legally committed cash relative to actually drawable finance, not accounting order-book growth alone. [S4,S5,S8; claims ledger]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Over five years, 5× and 10× require annual price growth of 37.97% and 58.49%, ending at ₹880.25 and ₹1,760.50. Using the conditional base-rescue share count/terminal claims, 12% EBITDA margin and 7x exit, fixed-claims algebra requires terminal revenue about ₹2,495.47 crore and ₹5,061.53 crore, respectively. These are feasibility yardsticks, not funded forecasts: faster growth would alter working capital, capacity, debt and dilution and must be re-solved. Enlarged nominal production capacity alone is only about double the old base, and EPC's clarified management 12–13% EBITDA and 8% PAT expectations are not achieved audited segment economics and do not establish collection quality. Even the optimistic modeled bull returns 29.96% annually, short of a fivefold five-year outcome. No evidence-based 5×/10× thesis is established. [S6,S8; model_results.json multibagger]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain current lender-wise utilized/undrawn amount, margin/drawing-power certificate, security eligibility, renewal dates and conditions. March starting bank ₹45.7042 crore against ₹83 crore sanction is not an October certificate; loss of roughly half the theoretical headroom breaks the central essential envelope.
2. Reconcile remaining EPC ex-GST book, certification, cash received, retention, guarantees, LD/termination terms and extensions. Baseline estimated remaining ₹314.8061 crore; verify completion against January nine-month and December one-year terms without presuming breach.
3. Track cumulative CFO and collection against PAT in the next audited interim/full-year release. FY24–26 CFO/PAT is −1.791x; another large absorption with growing advances keeps the cash cap in force. Sustained positive conversion, not a single release, is needed to lift CASH.
4. Age AR and inventory: March AR ₹95.5615 crore, 99.16% under six months; inventory ₹78.8634 crore with finished goods ₹44.7314 crore. Growing >6-month balances, disputed certificates or write-downs would worsen D/CASH.
5. Reconcile bank monthly stock statements to audited inventory, AR and AP, and explain the March differences before treating sanction as spendable cash.
6. Identify remaining adjacent-land purchase consideration and committed machinery payments after the June advance. Central essential bank headroom is ₹11.66 crore before extra financing cost, equivalent to about ₹11.30 crore additional cash commitment; hypothetical ₹15 crore additional obligation breaks it.
7. Verify production/customer approvals and utilization at new conductor/cable lines, not just nominal 56,000 km capacity. Watch H2 normalized EBITDA margin baseline 11.69% and EPC-specific margin/overruns.
8. Confirm latest promoter pledge/holding, related demand-loan movements and future capital issuance; current official shares 22,551,112, March promoter approximately 70%. Any discounted financing changes per-share returns.
9. Before implementation, obtain current BSE surveillance/settlement restrictions, bid–ask/depth and lot schedule; rerun ₹5 lakh and actual intended-position tests. A three-lot ₹422,520 or four-lot ₹563,360 position differs materially from the illustrative exact ₹5 lakh.
10. Recompute capital-cohort returns as plants mature: latest incremental 7.77% must improve toward/above the 12–15% cost range without excluding IPO funds or project capital. [S1,S3–S14,M1,M2]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold—unresolved; mixed-quality, capital-intensive growth/execution transition, not a proven compounder, not Avoid—governance, and not an evidenced financing failure. This is a research action category rather than an instruction to retain or trade an existing holding whose tax/portfolio context is unknown. Unrounded BQS 4.96 lies in the 4≤BQS<6 matrix quality band, GQS is capped at 5.0, and missing R/L prevent a complete price-attractiveness classification. No IAS ranking or buy/accumulate conclusion is supported.

Quality comparisons may be retained provisionally at Medium confidence because the central audited baseline is usable, with explicit history and judgement limits; all universe rankings await completion. First resolve current drawable credit, remaining signed EPC/land cash commitments, certificate timing and BSE implementation. Then replace counterfactual rescue with an evidenced funded base and rerun 15% hurdle/claims/dilution. ₹156.97 is only a conditional base-rescue hurdle crosscheck, not a standing order or safety threshold. Stronger price performance does not improve business quality; better certified cash conversion and mature incremental capital returns can. [Factor/gate audit and sections 10–13]

Verified figures, management statements, calculations and assumptions are separated in evidence_ledger.json. Material assumptions are 25% tax, normalized margins, future revenue/capex/ONWC, 5x/7x/9x exits, renewable ₹83 crore bank ceiling, rescue issue price/fees and essential EPC intensity/allocation. Current free cash, facility eligibility, project realization, future financing and post-March land obligations are not silently verified by an old annual report. Financial model values are INR crore; quote/lot tests INR; GST-inclusive awards are converted to ex-GST once.

Open questions: actual October bank usage/drawing power and renewals; full EPC milestone/termination/BG/retention and cash-to-complete schedule; certified completion/extensions; remaining adjacent-land consideration; product certifications/utilization; audit-to-bank differences; RHP-to-annual FY25 comparison and DSCR/IPO-fee definitions; September scanned pledge/ownership details; current BSE restrictions/spread/depth; reliable older primary history and common-date peer multiples. None is substituted with neutral scores. Earlier tax matters and reporting differences are not crimes or defaults without evidence. No information published after the cutoff is used to improve or condemn the thesis.

Reproduce in order: build_inputs.py; model.py; assemble_dossier.py; final QA script. All opening claims settle once through ONWC, payment, debt or terminal deduction, or an explicit unknown-obligation bound. Ordinary unfunded cases retain null IRRs; rescue scenarios are separate and uncommitted. Exact Decimal score audit, annual cash/debt/equity rollforwards, source snapshots and final artifact hashes are preserved for review. No Git, Library or public publication was performed.
